title: Game controller modification for fMRI hyperscanning experiments in a cooperative virtual reality environment
author: Trees, Snider, et al.

steps.title: Open controller and remove board
steps.instruction: Remove the controller back, fold out the smaller circuit board, and completely remove the circuit board from the housing, keeping all components attached to the buttons and plastic joystick covers.

steps.title: Desolder vibrator and joystick parts
steps.instruction: Using a soldering iron, desolder the two pairs of wires leading to the vibrator motors, the two adjacent resistors for vibrator function, the two joystick assemblies (bend back the orange potentiometers carefully to avoid breaking connections), and one LED.

steps.title: Remove joystick base and button
steps.instruction: Remove the white plastic base of the joystick assembly together with the attached button.

steps.title: Model and 3D‑print joystick housing
steps.instruction: Create a 3D model of the metal joystick housing and plastic base using SolidWorks 2013, then print a precise replica with a 3D Systems ProJet® 3510 HD printer using VisiJet M3 material or other MRI‑safe plastic such as ABS or PLA.

steps.title: Prepare stock joystick components
steps.instruction: Disassemble the stock joystick assemblies, retaining the plastic components and the single non‑magnetic metal axle; cut an ultra‑precision 302 stainless‑steel compression spring to the same size as the original spring.

steps.title: Assemble rebuilt joystick
steps.instruction: Glue a plastic block cut to the dimensions of the original button onto the base piece to support one joystick axle (the button is omitted because it contains magnetic metal), then reassemble the joystick using the printed housing and base, the cut stainless‑steel spring, and the remaining stock pieces; finally, glue the housing and base together on the outside, ensuring no glue enters the interior.

steps.title: Test joystick with web app
steps.instruction: Attach the rebuilt joystick assembly to the circuit board, secure the potentiometers to the new housing, and verify that buttons and potentiometers respond correctly using the Unity Web Player joystick test web application (http://dal‑acm.ca/∼dice/joytest/joystick%20test.html).

steps.title: Construct controller cable – first half
steps.instruction: Using a soldering iron, remove the stock USB wire connections; cut 20 ft (6.096 m) of Belden 8723 special‑purpose audio communication & instrumentation cable (2‑pair); strip and separate the wires at both ends; solder one wire of the first twisted pair to the D‑ connection and the other to D+; solder one wire of the second twisted pair to ground (DND) and the other to power (VOC); on the opposite end, solder the four wires to a D‑sub 25 connector using pins 1 (DND), 3 (D+), 5 (D‑), and 7 (VOC); any 4‑pin (or more) connector such as two BNCs or a serial port may be used; finally, solder a connection from the ground pin (1) to the metal housing of the D‑sub 25 connector to link room shielding to controller shielding (no external filter is used).

steps.title: Construct secondary D‑sub‑to‑USB cable
steps.instruction: Assemble a secondary cable that matches the USB wire configuration to the pins used in step 8, providing the connection from the MRI room wall pass‑through to the experiment computer.

steps.title: Apply conductive coating inside housing
steps.instruction: Drill a hole in the bottom half of the casing near the cable opening; tape off all holes and outer sides of each housing piece with painter’s tape; insert toothpicks into screw holes to prevent paint blockage; spray an even solid coat of Super Shield™ silver‑coated copper conductive coating on the interior of both halves, including the mating edges; wait 15 min and spray a second coat; wait 24 h, repeat the taping and spraying steps; finally, allow an additional 24 h for the coating to cure.

steps.title: Install brass bolt and nuts
steps.instruction: Insert a brass bolt into the drilled hole and secure tightly with a brass nut (circled in red); attach a second brass nut without fully tightening it.

steps.title: Reassemble controller housing
steps.instruction: Replace all button pieces into the controller housing, insert the circuit board back, secure the board with replacement 3/8″ slotted brass round‑headed screws, attach the naked shielding wire from the cable to the brass bolt and secure with the second nut, then reconnect the two halves of the housing and fasten with brass screws.

steps.title: Obtain scenario objects and actors
steps.instruction: Using VBS2’s development interface and object libraries, obtain the required objects, actors, and a suitable environment for the scenario (see Fig. 9A).

steps.title: Set situational logic and scripts
steps.instruction: Create an initialization script that runs when the scenario starts and additional .sqf script files containing needed functions; place all scripts in the same folder as the mission files.

steps.title: Bind controller keys to actions
steps.instruction: Through the VBS2 options menu, assign appropriate in‑game functions to each controller key.

steps.title: Create non‑verbal communication interface
steps.instruction: Develop separate VBS2 script functions to display text locked to avatar position, assign these functions to “User Defined Actions” in the script, and bind the user‑defined actions to the desired controller buttons via the options menu.

steps.title: Set up additional data logging
steps.instruction: Identify VBS2 scripting functions that interact with the native After Action Review (AAR) logger; within the initialization script, add events such as checkpoint reached, shots fired, and inter‑player signals to be logged.

steps.title: Start cooperative mission over LAN
steps.instruction: Initiate the cooperative mission using VBS2’s built‑in networking protocol over a local area network.

steps.title: Solder BNC to Teensy DAC
steps.instruction: Solder a BNC connector to the 12‑bit DAC channel (D) and ground (G) pins on the Teensy 3.1.

steps.title: Install Arduino IDE for Teensy
steps.instruction: Download the Arduino software from http://www.arduino.cc/en/Main/Software, select the appropriate download for your operating system, launch the installer, and follow the prompts.

steps.title: Install Teensyduino extension
steps.instruction: Download the Teensy extension from https://www.pjrc.com/teensy/td_download.html, select the download for your operating system, launch the installer, and follow the prompts.

steps.title: Connect Teensy via USB
steps.instruction: Connect the Teensy 3.1 to the computer with its mini‑USB cable (only one Teensy is required to trigger both scanners from the master experiment computer).

steps.title: Flash Teensy with custom code
steps.instruction: Program the Teensy 3.1 with custom firmware that provides a serial interface to receive commands and can generate a 10 ms square‑wave pulse.

steps.title: Connect VBS2 plugin to Teensy
steps.instruction: Use the custom VBS2 plugin to open a serial connection to the Teensy 3.1 and send a pulse over the BNC connector to both MRIs.

steps.title: Synchronize MRI start pulses
steps.instruction: Initialize the two MRIs simultaneously so that two consecutive 10 ms pulses, spaced 500 ms apart, start both scanners in sync from within the VBS2 environment.
